hints.title: Unsorted Insertion Scanning Obstacle
hints.text: Scanning the entire unsorted list repeatedly is inefficient. How can a sentinel node help you find the correct insertion slot for the next element in the sorted prefix?

hints.title: Sorted Prefix Boundary Invariant
hints.text: Maintain a sorted prefix ending at lastSorted. If curr.val is less than lastSorted.val, scan from dummy head to locate the first node with a larger value and insert curr.

hints.title: Sentinel Prefix Search Procedure
hints.text: Use dummy head pointing to head. Set lastSorted to head and curr to head.next. While curr exists: if lastSorted.val <= curr.val, advance lastSorted. Otherwise, find prev starting from dummy where prev.next.val > curr.val, splice curr between prev and prev.next, and update curr to lastSorted.next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Classic in-place insertion sort on a singly linked list in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unordered scanning and full list traversal on every node takes quadratic comparisons without early termination on already-sorted prefixes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Direct link splicing operates in O(1) auxiliary space without node array duplication.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Optimizing the sorted check (last_sorted.val <= curr.val) to achieve linear time on nearly sorted inputs.
